item: A host that writes the socket guard's words in its status line is its own failure, not the person's airplane mode (the wrapped-refusal alternative of _OFFLINE_RE spelled out)
summary: R616, OPEN_QUEUE 2026-11-08 item 42 (found by the read of R614's second PR). The second alternative of fetch_verdict._OFFLINE_RE read 'request error for <url>: ' followed by anything and then the socket guard's words, and urllib3 quotes a status line it could not parse (('Connection aborted.', BadStatusLine('<the host's line>'))), so a host that wrote the guard's words as its status line was read as the person's airplane mode: a calendar feed then stayed skipped_offline and never climbed its re-check ladder, and a hostile feed in the sample left the feed preflight incomplete on every run. Reproduced live with a loopback server answering with those words as its status line. The alternative now spells urllib3's construction out from its first word with no gap: the pool sentence with host and port, a path token with no space, '(Caused by NewConnectionError(' (optionally led by the ProxyError urllib3 gives when the guard refused a proxy that is not on loopback), the connection's host and port, then the guard's words, under the direct class names and the ones urllib3.contrib.socks gives over a SOCKS proxy (the protected transport, Tor); the host tokens take no whitespace, quote or backslash, as in the resolver alternative (R298). The independent security read found two more ways to the same place, both fixed here: the branch's first commit named only the direct classes, so a real Stop over Tor was no longer read as one (never on main) (checked through real PySocks 1.7.1 in a scratch path; it is not in the lock); and the fetcher wrote the caller's raw URL into the sentence, so a feed item's link that held spaces could continue in the guard's words and be read as airplane mode with the switch never engaged (reproduced end to end through EthicalFetcher.fetch, also on main). The fetcher now writes the URL through fetch_verdict.failure_url, which percent-encodes every character the reader's \S does not take and changes nothing else; the request is unchanged. tests/test_refusal_wrapped_shape.py (36 cases, one skips without PySocks) takes the real shapes from the real guard through real requests and urllib3 (https, http, a port, a refused proxy, through EthicalFetcher.fetch, and over SOCKS from the real urllib3 exception objects under contrib.socks's class names, read from its source as a drift pin); the live loopback reproductions (a status line, a feed link with spaces) and ten forged shapes are not read as offline. Passes on urllib3 2.7.0 (the lock) and 2.8.0. Twelve mutants are killed. Two independent security reads (R616): an Opus read, folded here, and the steward's. Left as they are, named: a loopback HTTP proxy's CONNECT refusal ('Connection aborted.', AirplaneModeError(...)) matches neither pattern (a false 'not offline', the safe direction; the recorders read the switch). Release-notes line: a server that answers with words copied from the app's airplane-mode refusal, or a feed whose links carry such words, is no longer mistaken for airplane mode, so its source is checked again like any other failing source.
